entry.title: When familiar sleep changes
entry.summary: The authors describe changing sleep as a time to notice what is different and offer needed support. Their developmental examples are possibilities, not an explanation for every waking baby.
entry.cue: Sleep has changed from the pattern you had come to know.
detail: The book mentions changes around eight months as one example, while also asking about comfort, surroundings and the baby’s response. More help may be needed for a time.
The authors return to observing readiness before reducing that help again. Their examples do not set a deadline for sleep to return to a previous pattern.

ageContext.bookAge: The sleep-change examples include around four, eight and twelve months.
ageContext.readiness: A familiar sleep pattern has changed and more support may be needed.
ageContext.note: The book also gives an example around twelve months. Its examples are possibilities to consider, not a schedule of sleep changes.

displayContext.footer: You don’t need a different home. Start with what you have.
displayContext.colophon: Original summaries inspired by The Montessori Baby and The Montessori Toddler. Open any idea for its book references. The illustration is an invitation to explore, rather than a room to reproduce. Follow your child’s pace.
